Class 5 · Chapter 1 of 10

Large numbers and place-value clues

Read seven- and eight-digit values and justify comparison or rounding.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

By the end I can…

  • I can build and compare large numbers.
  • I can round and solve digit clues.
  • I can use Roman numerals.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 5

Eight places

An eight-digit number has crores, ten lakhs, lakhs, ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.

In 35,207,184 the first digit 3 is worth thirty million.

In the Indian system it is written 3,52,07,184.

Screen 2 of 5

Read and name big numbers

Group the digits from the right: 3 crore, 52 lakh, 07 thousand and 184.

Say it: three crore, fifty-two lakh, seven thousand, one hundred eighty-four.

A zero keeps a place, but we do not say it.

Screen 3 of 5

Compare and order

More digits means a bigger number.

If the digits are equal in number, compare from the left.

Order 18,194, 34,238 and 83,119 from least to greatest.

Screen 4 of 5

Round to the nearest ten

Look at the ones digit. 5 or more rounds up. 4 or fewer rounds down.

245 is halfway between 240 and 250.

We round halfway numbers up, so 245 rounds to 250.

Screen 5 of 5

Roman numerals

C is 100, L is 50, X is 10, V is 5 and I is 1. D is 500.

Write the biggest parts first: 478 is 400 + 70 + 8.

That is CD, LXX and VIII: CDLXXVIII.

Words to know
place value
What a digit is worth because of its place. In 3,52,07,184 the 3 is worth 3 crore.
lakh
One lakh is 1,00,000. It has 6 digits.
crore
One crore is 1,00,00,000. It has 8 digits.
rounding
Changing a number to the nearest ten, hundred or thousand.

Chapter passed. Next: Solve stories with factors and multiples

For parents

What your child learns

To make the greatest number, put the largest digit in the highest place. Clues about multiples, digit sums and ranges narrow the choices. A multiple of 6 is even and also a multiple of 3.

A common slip

Children often check one clue only. A number must fit all clues. Test each choice against every clue one at a time.

5-minute home activity: Number clues

  1. Write 5 digits on paper cards.
  2. Make the greatest and the smallest number.
  3. Write three clues for a 6-digit number.
  4. Test a guess against each clue.
